corrections.baseline: Cairo 1.9.6, Skia (circa May 2010, CPU raster backend), Qt 4.5.x, Direct2D and the OpenVG 1.1 reference implementation (the nvpr_svg comparison backends in the NVprSDK)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (search summaries of the blocked paper PDF and ResearchGate page): the paper gives performance ratios of NV_path_rendering at 16 samples per pixel over Cairo, Skia, Qt, Direct2D and the OpenVG reference implementation for SVG scenes at window sizes from 100x100 to 1100x1100; one snippet attributes 8.69 ms at 1000x1000 with 16 samples against Cairo's 909 ms at 1000x1000 to a complex clipping scene (about 105x, derived from snippet data). The ratio tables themselves were not seen.
corrections.hardware: GeForce 650 GPU and an unnamed 'fast Core i7' CPU for the ratio benchmarks; a GeForce 560M laptop for the Snail Bob (5 ms) and SIGGRAPH web page (4.8 ms) frame timings (all per search snippets of the paper)
corrections.caveats: Paper-only entry for the research section. The paper PDF (developer.download.nvidia.com), the GTC 2012 slides and ResearchGate are blocked, so all numbers are from search-result snippets. NV_path_rendering is implemented inside NVIDIA's proprietary driver, so the renderer itself cannot be copied; only the SDK example code is public. An unofficial mirror of the July 2011 NVprSDK (github.com/victusfate/nvpr_demo, 1 star, no license file seen) carries nvpr_svg with -benchmark (best frames/second over 6-second intervals) and a key to benchmark the Qt/Cairo/Skia software renderer, but no recorded results. The CPU baselines are 2009-2010 versions (Skia's CPU raster path, not Ganesh/Graphite), the README notes Cairo 1.9.6 had a path-clipping bug, and the hardware is 2012-era. NVIDIA-only (GeForce 8 or later, driver 275.33+).

notes: Paper and comparison harness confirmed as real; numbers remain snippet-only, so C. A paper-access retier could move it to B. Skia has since dropped its NVPR backend, so the incumbent comparison is historical.
